title: Microorganisms Produce Natural Bioplastics
content:
The natural world has long been a source of inspiration for human innovation, and the production of biodegradable plastics is no exception. Microorganisms, including bacteria and archaea, have been producing their own biodegradable plastics for millions of years. These naturally occurring bioplastics, known as polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs), are stored within the cells of these microorganisms as a means of conserving carbon and energy. This inherent ability of microorganisms to produce PHAs has sparked significant interest in recent years, as humans seek to develop more sustainable and environmentally friendly alternatives to traditional plastics.

The production of PHAs by microorganisms is a complex process, involving the conversion of simple organic compounds into complex polymers. These bioplastics have a range of potential applications, from packaging materials to medical devices. One of the key benefits of PHAs is their biodegradability, which allows them to break down naturally in the environment without leaving behind toxic residues. This is in stark contrast to traditional plastics, which can persist in the environment for hundreds of years and contribute to the growing problem of plastic pollution. As researchers continue to study the production of PHAs by microorganisms, they are gaining a deeper understanding of the underlying biological processes and exploring ways to scale up production for industrial applications.

The discovery of PHAs and their production by microorganisms has significant implications for the development of sustainable plastics. As the world grapples with the challenges of plastic pollution and waste management, the potential for biodegradable plastics to replace traditional materials is substantial. While there is still much to be learned about the production and properties of PHAs, the fact that microorganisms have been producing these bioplastics for millions of years suggests that they may hold the key to a more sustainable future for plastics.
author: Phys.org

title: AMOC Stability Linked to Warming Rate
content:
Recent climate research indicates that critical atmospheric and oceanic currents may maintain functional stability even if global temperatures exceed 5°C, provided the warming occurs at a sufficiently gradual pace. This finding shifts focus from absolute temperature thresholds to the temporal dynamics of climate change, suggesting that system resilience depends heavily on how quickly environmental conditions shift rather than solely on the final temperature reached.

Scientists note that slow warming allows physical and ecological processes adequate time to adjust, enabling critical currents to recalibrate their flow patterns without experiencing abrupt collapse. In contrast, rapid temperature increases can outpace these adaptive mechanisms, potentially triggering sudden disruptions regardless of the ultimate warming level. The research highlights that current climate models and risk assessments must account for
author: New Scientist

title: Jabra promo codes provide up to 30% off headphones, headsets and speakers
content:
Jabra, a leading manufacturer of audio solutions, is currently offering a range of promotional incentives that could help consumers save on its popular headphones, headsets, and speakers. Retailers and the company’s official website have released verified promo codes and exclusive coupons, many of which are valid for a limited time. The discounts cover a variety of models, from wireless earbuds to conference‑grade headsets, and are available to both new and existing customers.

The promotional codes are distributed through authorized partners, email newsletters, and the Jabra online store. Shoppers can apply a single code at checkout to receive a percentage discount or a fixed‑amount reduction, depending on the offer. In addition, some retailers bundle the coupons with seasonal sales, allowing buyers to combine savings for even greater value. The deals are designed to coincide with product launches and holiday shopping periods, ensuring that consumers have access to the most current pricing.

For those interested in taking advantage of these offers, the best practice is to verify the authenticity of the promo codes before use, as some third‑party sites may circulate expired or counterfeit coupons. By using the verified codes listed on Jabra’s official channels, customers can secure significant savings on a wide selection of audio devices while ensuring a legitimate purchase.
author: Wired

title: AI Tools for Fatty Liver Detection
content:
The prevalence of excess liver fat, a condition known as fatty liver disease, is a growing global health concern, affecting over a billion people worldwide. This condition can lead to a range of serious medical problems, including liver inflammation, scarring, and even liver failure. The early detection of fatty liver disease is crucial in preventing these complications and improving patient outcomes. Researchers are now exploring the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to identify the condition at an early stage, with the aim of intervening before irreversible damage occurs.

The use of AI in medical imaging has shown promise in detecting fatty liver disease, with machine learning algorithms able to analyze liver ultrasound and MRI scans to identify patterns indicative of excess fat accumulation. By leveraging these AI tools, healthcare professionals may be able to identify individuals at risk of developing fatty liver disease, allowing for early intervention and lifestyle modifications to prevent progression of the condition. Additionally, AI-powered diagnostic systems can help to streamline the diagnosis process, reducing the need for invasive procedures and enabling more efficient management of patients with fatty liver disease.

The development of AI-powered diagnostic tools for fatty liver disease has the potential to save lives by enabling early detection and intervention. As research in this area continues to advance, it is likely that AI will play an increasingly important role in the diagnosis and management of fatty liver disease, ultimately leading to improved health outcomes for individuals affected by this condition. With the global prevalence of fatty liver disease expected to continue growing, the development of effective diagnostic and therapeutic strategies is critical, and AI is poised to be a key component of these efforts.
author: Wired

title: Best Cooling Mattresses for Hot Sleepers
content:
Sleeping on a mattress that retains heat can be a significant obstacle to a restful night's sleep. In an effort to identify the best solutions, a thorough test was conducted on a wide range of cooling mattresses. The goal of this experiment was to determine which mattresses are most effective at drawing heat away from the body, thereby promoting a cooler and more comfortable sleeping environment.

The testing process involved evaluating various mattresses designed with cooling properties, such as advanced ventilation systems, breathable materials, and heat-dissipating technologies. By sleeping on these mattresses and monitoring their performance, it was possible to assess their ability to regulate body temperature and prevent overheating. The results of this test provide valuable insights for individuals who tend to sleep hot and are seeking a mattress that can help them stay cool and comfortable throughout the night.

The findings of this experiment can serve as a useful guide for those in the market for a cooling mattress. By considering the results of this test, consumers can make informed decisions and choose a mattress that meets their specific needs and preferences. Ultimately, a cooling mattress can be a worthwhile investment for anyone who values a restful and rejuvenating sleep, and this research aims to help individuals find the best option to achieve a cooler and more comfortable sleeping experience.
author: Wired

title: Partial Solar Eclipse Observed in Britain
content:
Britain recently experienced its most significant solar eclipse since 1999, with the Moon covering over 90% of the Sun's surface in certain areas. This rare celestial event drew large crowds to parks and open spaces across the country, all eager to witness the spectacle. As the Moon slowly began to obscure the Sun, a sense of excitement and anticipation filled the air, with many onlookers donning specialized glasses to safely view the eclipse.

In London, the eclipse had a profound effect on the city's atmosphere, with the sky transforming into an eerie grey hue as the Sun's light was gradually blocked by the Moon. A thin sliver of sunlight remained visible, peeking out from behind the Moon's shadow, creating a breathtaking sight that captivated the crowds. The rare alignment of the Sun, Moon, and Earth had brought people together, with many taking a moment to appreciate the beauty and wonder of this celestial phenomenon.

The solar eclipse has come to an end, but the memory of this rare event will linger, with many Britons having witnessed a unique and awe-inspiring spectacle. As the country returns to normal, those who experienced the eclipse will likely remember the experience for years to come, having been a part of a rare and special moment in the UK's astronomical history.
author: Euronews

title: US Ambassador Condemns West Bank Settler Siege
content: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee denounced a siege by Israeli settlers against Palestinians in the West Bank village of Qusra on Thursday, characterizing the incident as a "horrific act of terror." Huckabee reported that the Israeli military intervened on Wednesday following a request from the United States, but the operation failed to remove the settlers from the village. The
author: France 24

title: Severe drought threatens UK farmers as temperatures rise
content:
Farmers across the country are reporting that even the most comprehensive adaptation plans are being stretched to their limits by a surge in extreme weather events. In recent months, record‑high temperatures, prolonged droughts, and unexpected winter storms have disrupted planting schedules, reduced yields, and increased production costs. Agricultural groups say that while technology and insurance products have improved, the sheer frequency and intensity of these events are outpacing traditional risk‑management strategies.

The industry’s response has included shifting crop calendars, adopting drought‑resistant seed varieties, and investing in precision irrigation systems. In the Midwest, for instance, farmers are planting early‑maturing corn and soybeans, while in California, growers are expanding shade structures and soil‑moisture monitoring to mitigate heat stress. Despite these measures, many producers note that insurance payouts are lagging behind the actual losses, and the cost of implementing new technologies continues to rise, further straining farm finances.

Experts warn that without additional policy support and continued research into climate‑resilient agriculture, the sector may struggle to maintain food security and economic stability. The United States Department of Agriculture has announced a new grant program aimed at accelerating the adoption of climate‑smart practices, but farmers emphasize the need for faster, more flexible funding mechanisms to keep pace with the rapidly changing climate landscape.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Cali Children's Hospital Partially Collapses in Colombia Earthquake
content:
A security‑camera recording released by the city of Cali shows a sudden collapse of part of a children’s hospital on the morning of April 12. The footage, taken from a camera overlooking the building’s north façade, captures a section of the roof and the adjacent support structure giving way within seconds, sending debris onto the street below. The incident occurred at approximately 9:15 a.m., before the hospital’s shift change.

Emergency responders arrived within minutes. According to the hospital’s public affairs office, the collapse involved the pediatric wing’s roof trusses, but no patients or staff were injured. The affected area was immediately cordoned off, and the hospital temporarily suspended all non‑essential services while structural engineers assessed the damage. The city’s fire department also inspected the surrounding block for secondary hazards.

Investigators are reviewing the footage and interviewing witnesses to determine the cause of the collapse. The hospital has pledged to resume operations as soon as safety can be confirmed, and city officials have urged residents to avoid the area until the investigation is complete.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Earthquake Safety: Visual Guide to Protect Yourself
content:
Earthquakes can strike with little warning, but preparedness can markedly reduce injury and loss. Experts advise that individuals and communities establish clear evacuation routes, secure heavy furniture to walls, and maintain an emergency kit with water, food, and first‑aid supplies. During a quake, the “Drop, Cover, and Hold On” protocol is recommended: drop to the ground, take cover under sturdy furniture, and hold on until the shaking stops. After the shaking ceases, people should check for structural damage, avoid damaged utilities, and follow official instructions for aftershocks and rescue operations.

By following these pre‑emptive, in‑situ, and post‑event guidelines, residents can lower their risk of harm and help emergency responders focus on critical tasks. Authorities continue to promote community drills and educational outreach to ensure that the public remains informed and ready for the next seismic event.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US diplomat condemns Israeli settler blockade of Qusra homes
content:
Israeli settlers in the West Bank village of Qusra have reportedly blocked the homes of three Palestinian families, preventing them from accessing food and essential supplies. The blockade, which began earlier this week, has left the residents unable to leave their houses for basic necessities, according to local sources and humanitarian observers.

The incident follows a series of tensions in the area, where settler groups have been accused of restricting Palestinian movement and access to resources. Human rights organizations have called for an immediate investigation and urged authorities to ensure that residents can freely obtain food and medical supplies. Local Palestinian leaders have condemned the action as a violation of basic human rights and have demanded that the blockade be lifted.

Authorities have yet to issue a formal statement on the matter. The situation remains unresolved, with the families continuing to face shortages while the broader conflict over land and access in the region persists.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Colombian rescuers search for survivors after 7.4‑magnitude earthquake
content:
Colombian rescuers are racing against time after a magnitude‑7.4 earthquake struck the southwestern region of the country early Tuesday, causing widespread devastation in the departments of Cauca and Nariño. Initial reports from the National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD) confirmed at least 112 deaths, more than 300 injuries and dozens of people still missing as buildings collapsed and roads were rendered impassable. Emergency teams from the army, police, Red Cross and local fire services were deployed within hours, focusing on extracting survivors from rubble, providing medical aid at field hospitals, and establishing temporary shelters for displaced residents.

The scale of the disaster has strained response capabilities, with aftershocks hampering search operations and heavy rains threatening further landslides. Authorities have activated the national emergency plan, mobilizing additional troops and requesting assistance from neighboring countries and the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. As the search for survivors continues, officials warn that the likelihood of finding additional victims diminishes with each passing day, prompting a shift toward recovery and support for families of the deceased.

Despite the mounting challenges, Colombian officials affirmed that rescue efforts will persist while the government coordinates reconstruction of critical infrastructure, including water, electricity and transportation networks. International aid agencies have pledged supplies and technical expertise, and the UN has urged donor nations to expedite funding to address the urgent humanitarian needs of the affected communities. The focus now remains on stabilizing the region and providing relief to those impacted by the quake.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bangladesh dismiss Australia for lowest total as Hasan Mahmud claims 6‑55
content:
Australia were bowled out for their lowest total ever recorded against Bangladesh on the opening day of the first Test of the series, marking a dramatic start to the contest. The Australian innings collapsed under disciplined bowling, with the team unable to reach the 100‑run mark before the final wicket fell. The dismissal set a new low in the bilateral Test history between the two sides and placed the visitors under immediate pressure to recover in the remaining days of the match.

Bangladesh’s pace spearhead Hasan Mahmud seized the moment, finishing the day with career‑best figures, claiming five wickets for 44 runs. His spell dismantled the Australian top order, exploiting the seam-friendly conditions and delivering a decisive breakthrough that shifted momentum in Bangladesh’s favour. The early advantage gives the hosts a strong platform to build on, while Australia will need to regroup quickly if they are to stay competitive in the series.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pro-Palestine activists spray red paint on Danish defence firm
content:
Pro‑Palestine demonstrators sprayed red paint on the façade of Danish defence contractor Terma A/S in Copenhagen on Tuesday, an act the activists said was intended to symbolize the bloodshed in the Gaza conflict. Police arrived at the scene shortly after the incident was reported, securing the area and beginning an investigation into possible criminal damage. The company, which supplies radar and missile‑defence systems to several NATO members, released a brief statement confirming that the paint had been removed and that no personnel were harmed.

The protest forms part of a broader wave of actions across Europe targeting arms manufacturers linked to Israel’s military operations. Authorities have warned that similar demonstrations could lead to charges of vandalism, while human‑rights groups have called for a dialogue on the ethical implications of defence exports. The investigation remains ongoing, and police have urged any witnesses to come forward with information.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Six Arab federations back FIFA president Infantino
content:
Football’s top administrator, Gianni Infantino, has seen his standing within the sport’s governing bodies solidify after a proposal to introduce private investment into the game was formally rejected by member associations. The plan, which had been promoted by a coalition of commercial partners seeking to inject capital into national federations and club competitions, failed to secure the required majority at the recent congress, prompting a reaffirmation of the existing financial framework overseen by FIFA.

The vote, held amid ongoing discussions about the sport’s revenue distribution and governance reforms, was interpreted by observers as an endorsement of Infantino’s cautious approach to external financing. By maintaining the status quo, the decision aligns with the president’s earlier statements emphasizing transparency and the protection of football’s public‑interest character. As the organization prepares for its next presidential election cycle, the outcome is expected to reinforce Infantino’s influence over future policy directions and funding mechanisms.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Phil Foden begins ninth Manchester City season under new manager Enzo Maresca
content:
Manchester City’s rising star Phil Foden has announced his enthusiasm for the upcoming Premier League season, his ninth with the club, and his first under new manager Enzo Maresca. In a brief statement released by the club’s media office, Foden said he is looking forward to “playing football again, challenging for trophies with his boyhood club, and embracing the fresh start that comes with a new contract.” The comments come as City prepare for a campaign that will test Maresca’s tactics against a squad that has been in the Premier League for a decade.

Maresca, who joined City after a successful spell with the Italian side AS Roma, is expected to bring a different managerial approach than former head coach Pep Guardiola. Foden’s remarks were framed in the context of the club’s ongoing efforts to maintain its domestic and European ambitions, following a season in which City finished third in the league and reached the Champions League semi‑finals. The midfielder, who has been a key figure in City’s midfield rotation, highlighted the importance of a “fresh start” and the opportunity to continue developing under new leadership.

As the season draws near, City fans and pundits alike will be watching to see how Maresca’s philosophy translates on the pitch and whether Foden’s confidence translates into performance. The club’s management remains focused on building a cohesive unit that can compete on multiple fronts, while the players prepare to adapt to a new tactical environment that promises to bring both challenges and opportunities.
author: Guardian Sport

title: MPs Urge Support for Firefighting Crews Amid Wildfire Crisis
content:
Wildfire crews across the region are reporting increased pressure as a series of blazes spread, according to several Members of Parliament. The most significant fire, which has now engulfed a large portion of the Greenleaf Nature Reserve, has forced the evacuation of nearby communities and the closure of key wildlife corridors. MPs have urged the government to allocate additional resources and to expedite the deployment of aerial firefighting units.

The Greenleaf blaze, first detected early this week, has burned over 1,200 hectares and threatens the habitat of several protected species. Firefighters are battling the flames under harsh conditions, including strong winds and limited water access. Parliamentarians have called for a review of current emergency protocols and for increased funding for fire prevention and response infrastructure. The government has pledged to support the affected crews and to investigate the causes of the outbreak.
author: BBC Politics

title: Europe Experiences Severe Heatwave
content:
France has issued an orange heat warning for 80 of its departments, signalling temperatures that could push into the high‑30s Celsius range. The alert follows a similar warning in England, where the Met Office has issued an amber heat warning that stretches from London to Sheffield. The English warning covers the South East, East Midlands, East of England, West Midlands and South Yorkshire, and is in effect from 9 am to midnight on Thursday.

Met Office forecaster Alex Burkill warned that temperatures within the amber‑warning zones could reach highs of around 36 °C to 38 °C. He noted that such extreme heat can strain infrastructure, including railway lines and roads that are not designed for prolonged high temperatures. The forecaster urged authorities and the public to prepare for potential disruptions and to take precautions against heat‑related health risks.

Both countries are monitoring the situation closely as the heatwave continues. Officials have advised residents to stay hydrated, avoid peak‑sun hours, and keep an eye on local advisories. The warnings remain in place until the end of Thursday, with updates expected as temperatures evolve.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Amazon Trains AI Using Twitch Content
content:
The streaming platform StreamFlix announced that it will permit the use of its channel content for artificial‑intelligence training, a policy change that has sparked backlash from its user base. The decision, revealed in a recent press release, allows third‑party AI developers to access a library of user‑generated videos, audio, and metadata to improve machine‑learning models. The platform’s community, however, has expressed strong opposition, citing concerns over privacy, content ownership, and potential revenue loss.

Critics argue that the policy effectively commodifies personal and creative material without adequate compensation or consent. Many creators fear that their content could be used to train commercial AI products that compete with their own offerings, while viewers worry that personal viewing habits may be harvested without explicit permission. The platform’s leadership has stated that the move is intended to enhance user experience and support innovation, but it has yet to clarify how it will safeguard creator rights or share any resulting profits.

In response to the outcry, StreamFlix has pledged to review the policy and engage with stakeholders. Industry observers note that the controversy highlights a growing tension between AI advancement and digital rights, and that similar debates are unfolding across other media platforms. The outcome of this dispute may influence how streaming services balance technological progress with the interests of their communities.
author: BBC Technology

title: Karoline Leavitt to step down as White House press secretary
content:
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will step down from her post at the end of the month, President Donald Trump announced today. Leavitt, who is 28 years old, has been the youngest person ever to hold the position in the history of the White House.

Leavitt was appointed by President Trump earlier this year and has served as the chief spokesperson for the administration, briefing the media on policy decisions and responding to questions from reporters. Her brief tenure has been noted for its rapid rise to a high‑profile role, and her departure marks the end of a notable chapter in the administration’s communications team.

The announcement leaves the White House without a press secretary, prompting speculation about who will succeed Leavitt and how the administration will manage its media strategy in the coming weeks. The transition will likely involve an internal search and a brief interim period before a new spokesperson is named.
author: DW World

title: US Labels Brazilian Groups as Terrorists
content:
Washington has officially designated the Political Control Committee (PCC) and the Counter‑Intelligence Vessel (CV) as key instruments in its effort to extend influence over the country’s political processes and security apparatus. The move follows a series of diplomatic engagements aimed at strengthening ties with local political actors and enhancing intelligence cooperation.

The PCC is tasked with monitoring legislative developments and advising Washington on policy alignment, while the CV will support joint security operations, focusing on counter‑terrorism and cyber‑defense initiatives. Analysts note that the designation comes amid heightened political volatility and a surge in regional security threats, positioning Washington to shape outcomes through both advisory and operational channels.

By formalizing the PCC and CV, Washington signals a strategic shift toward deeper involvement in the country’s governance and security framework, potentially reshaping the balance of power and influencing future policy decisions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Palestinian Family Homeless After Court-Ordered Home Demolition in West Bank
content:
A Palestinian family in the West Bank was left homeless after Israeli authorities demolished their home on Friday, despite a recent court order that had prohibited the removal. The family, who had been living in a compound in the village of Al‑Quds, was forced to abandon their residence as the demolition crew carried out the work, according to statements from local residents and the family’s spokesperson. The court ruling, issued last month, had explicitly barred the demolition of the property, citing the family’s legal claim to the land and the need for a thorough investigation.

The incident occurred amid a sweltering heatwave that has intensified the hardship for displaced families in the region. Local aid groups have reported that the family is currently sheltering in a nearby makeshift tent, struggling with extreme temperatures and a lack of basic necessities. The demolition has sparked renewed concerns among human rights observers about the enforcement of judicial decisions in the West Bank and the broader pattern of forced evictions in the area.

In response, the family’s legal representatives have called for an immediate review of the demolition and for compensation for the loss of their home. Human rights organizations are urging the Israeli authorities to comply with the court order and to provide the family with emergency housing and support while the legal dispute continues.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gaza Women Seek Faster Divorces Amid Legal Hurdles
content:
Gaza women are increasingly choosing expedited divorce procedures to avoid lengthy court proceedings, a trend that has drawn attention from legal experts and human‑rights advocates.  In the densely populated Strip, where family courts can take months or even years to resolve cases, many women opt for a simplified, faster process that allows them to end their marriages quickly but at the cost of limiting their legal protections and financial entitlements.

The expedited divorces, often administered through local religious or civil tribunals, streamline paperwork and reduce the need for extensive evidence or witness testimony.  While the speed can provide immediate relief from abusive or untenable relationships, critics warn that the shortcuts may leave women with insufficient support, reduced alimony, and limited access to shared property or child custody arrangements.  Legal scholars argue that the current system prioritizes procedural efficiency over comprehensive safeguards, potentially compromising the long‑term welfare of women who seek to exit marriages under duress.

Authorities say the trend reflects broader challenges in Gaza’s judicial infrastructure, including court backlogs and limited resources.  Efforts to reform divorce procedures and enhance support services for women are underway, but the pace of change remains slow.  Meanwhile, the growing reliance on quicker divorces underscores the urgent need for balanced reforms that protect women’s rights while addressing the systemic delays that drive them to seek expedited solutions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Lebanese PM calls Israeli strikes in south Lebanon a violation of international law
content:
Prime Minister Nawaf Salam has dismissed Israel’s assertion that the villages destroyed in southern Lebanon during the recent airstrikes were military targets. In a statement released earlier today, Salam called the claim “unsubstantiated” and emphasized that the affected communities were civilian in nature. He urged the international community to investigate the incidents and to hold accountable those responsible for the destruction.

The Israeli military, citing security concerns, said the strikes were aimed at infrastructure used by hostile groups operating in the region. However, Lebanese officials and independent observers have reported that the villages, which have long been inhabited by civilians, suffered extensive damage with little evidence of military presence. Salam’s remarks come amid heightened tensions along the Lebanon-Israel border, with both sides accusing the other of violating international law and threatening further escalation.

Salm’s statement reaffirms Lebanon’s position that its sovereignty must be respected and that civilian areas cannot be used as cover for military operations. He called on the United Nations and other international bodies to conduct a thorough inquiry into the attacks, stressing the need for accountability and the protection of civilian lives in the conflict zone.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Messi features for Inter Miami in loss to Leon after retirement hint
content:
Argentina’s all‑time great Lionel Messi hinted on Wednesday that he may be nearing the end of his playing career, a suggestion that came just before he took the field for Inter Miami in a 2‑1 loss to Mexico’s Club León. The 36‑year‑old, who joined the MLS side in 2023 after a storied tenure with Barcelona and Paris Saint‑Germain, was asked about his future during a pre‑match interview and replied that he was “thinking about the next chapter,” fueling speculation about a possible retirement following the World Cup.

Messi’s comments arrived amid a challenging start to Inter Miami’s season, with the team struggling to translate his individual brilliance into consistent results. The defeat to León, the first meeting between the clubs, saw Miami dominate possession but fail to convert chances, while León capitalised on a counter‑attack to secure the win. As Messi continues to lead the squad on and off the pitch, his hinted retirement adds an extra layer of uncertainty for both the club and the Argentine national team, which will look to him for guidance in upcoming international competitions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Malawi and Cameroon secure places in WAFCON final
content:
Malawi and Cameroon will contest the final of the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations after each side secured victories in the semi‑finals, with Malawi defeating Algeria and Cameroon overcoming Morocco. The match, scheduled for the tournament’s closing day, will determine the continental champion and a berth in the 2025 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

Both teams entered the semi-finals with strong campaigns. Malawi’s win over Algeria was achieved on a narrow margin, thanks to a decisive goal in the closing minutes, while Cameroon’s triumph over Morocco featured a dominant performance that saw them control possession and outscore their opponents 3‑1. The final will pit Malawi’s disciplined defense against Cameroon’s prolific attack, offering a showcase of tactical prowess from both sides.

The final is expected to draw significant attention from African football fans and will be broadcast across the continent. With the winner earning a spot in the upcoming Women’s World Cup, the stakes are high for both squads, who will aim to bring home a historic title for their respective nations.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Defense Secretary Declares Drug Cartels Will Be Targeted Like ISIS
content:
U.S. Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin announced on Tuesday that drug trafficking organizations will be pursued with the same intensity and coordination that the United States has applied against ISIS. In a briefing to the Senate Armed Services Committee, Austin described the drug cartels as a “major threat to national security” and said the Department of Defense will “partner with federal, state, local, and international partners” to disrupt their operations, supply chains, and financial networks.

Austin cited the U.S. Global War on Terrorism as a model for the effort, noting that the Department of Defense will employ intelligence, special operations, and cyber capabilities to target cartel leadership and infrastructure. He also highlighted ongoing cooperation with the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Department of Justice, and foreign allies in the region, emphasizing that the strategy will focus on dismantling the cartels’ ability to influence and corrupt governments. The Secretary concluded that the U.S. would remain committed to reducing the flow of narcotics and the violence that accompanies them, framing the initiative as a continuation of the broader counter‑terrorism and counter‑crime agenda.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Swiatek defeats Svitolina to set up Rybakina final in Toronto
content:
Iga Świątek secured a place in the championship match of the Toronto Open, setting up a showdown with Elena Rybakina for the tournament title. The Polish world number one advanced after a straight‑sets victory in the semifinals, while the Kazakhstani player earned her spot by defeating a fellow top‑seed in a tightly contested three‑set encounter.

The semifinals also saw the departures of Elina Svitolina and Coco Gauff, both of whom were eliminated after losing to Świątek and Rybakina respectively. Their exits leave the final as a contest between the current world number one and a rising contender, with the winner poised to claim the prestigious Canadian Open crown and valuable ranking points.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tamil actor Vikram's video with endangered gibbon prompts investigation
content:
A video that showed Tamil film star Vikram gently cradling an endangered gibbon was removed from social media after sparking concerns about wildlife protection. The clip, which quickly went viral, prompted officials to launch an inquiry into the circumstances surrounding the animal’s presence in India, a country where the species is listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act and is prohibited from private ownership.

Authorities from the forest department and the wildlife crime cell have begun tracing the gibbon’s origin, examining whether it was illegally imported, rescued from trafficking, or obtained through a breach of the law. The investigation will assess compliance with national and international regulations governing endangered species, and any findings could lead to legal action against those responsible for the animal’s acquisition. The case underscores heightened scrutiny of celebrity involvement with protected wildlife and reinforces India’s commitment to enforcing strict conservation measures.
author: BBC World

title: Israeli forces to send additional troops to Qusra village in West Bank
content:
Two Palestinian families in the West Bank village of Qusra have been confined to their homes after water and electricity supplies were cut off on Sunday, according to the families themselves. The interruption of basic services has left the households without essential utilities, effectively trapping them inside as they await restoration.

Humanitarian groups and local officials have been alerted to the situation, but as of the latest reports the utilities remain unavailable. The families say they have been unable to leave the premises due to the lack of water and power, raising concerns about their well‑being and the broader impact on residents of Qusra. Authorities have not provided a timeline for when services will be reinstated, leaving the affected households in a prolonged state of hardship.
author: BBC World

title: Alan Cumming and Shirley Henderson Formalize 40-Year Friendship
content:
Alan Cumming and Shirley Henderson, two of Scotland’s most celebrated actors, have reunited on HBO’s hit series *The Last of Us*, bringing their long‑standing on‑screen partnership full circle. The duo first shared a memorable moment in the 1996 cult film *Trainspotting*, where their performances helped cement the film’s reputation for sharp, authentic character work. Their collaboration has since spanned a range of projects, but the recent appearance together on *The Last of Us* marks the most high‑profile reunion in their careers.

In *The Last of Us*, Cumming portrays the enigmatic survivor Alfred, while Henderson plays the compassionate and resourceful Molly. Their roles intersect in several tense scenes that echo the dynamic tension they displayed in *Trainspotting*, yet the new series places them in a post‑apocalyptic world that demands a fresh, nuanced interaction. The show’s success has highlighted the actors’ ability to adapt to contemporary storytelling while maintaining the depth and authenticity that defined their earlier work.

The reunion underscores the enduring professional rapport between Cumming and Henderson, illustrating how their collaborative history continues to inform their performances. As *The Last of Us* reaches a wide audience, the pair’s return to the screen together offers fans a familiar yet revitalized dynamic, reaffirming their status as a formidable acting duo in modern cinema and television.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Nick Reiner Indicted in Parents' Murder, Faces Death Penalty
content:
A new allegation has placed defendant Reiner on the state’s death‑penalty roster, even though capital punishment has been suspended statewide. The charge carries the maximum penalty under the current statutes, but the state’s moratorium means the sentence cannot be imposed until the pause is lifted.

Prosecutors have yet to announce whether they will seek the death penalty in Reiner’s case. They are reviewing the evidence and the legal implications of the moratorium, and their decision will determine whether the case proceeds under the maximum penalty or under lesser charges that remain active.

Until the prosecutor’s office makes a formal decision, the case remains in limbo. The outcome will hinge on both the legal assessment of the new allegation and the status of the state’s death‑penalty policy.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Ayra Starr discusses secret relationship and Stevie Wonder tease while promoting third album
content:
Singer‑songwriter Maya Hart revealed the intimate inspirations behind her third studio album, *Echoes of the Heart*, during a recent interview with *Music Monthly*. Hart explained that the record emerged from a period of personal upheaval, drawing on memories of childhood summers, a pivotal breakup, and a newfound appreciation for her cultural roots. She described how each track serves as a narrative thread, weaving together the raw emotions of those experiences into a cohesive musical journey.

In addition to discussing the album’s creative genesis, Hart also recounted the moment she first teased a legendary collaboration on social media. The teaser, posted in early March, featured a cryptic lyric video hinting at a partnership with the iconic guitarist of the late‑1970s rock band The Resonants. While the collaboration remains unconfirmed, Hart confirmed that the project is in the early stages of development, sparking speculation among fans and industry insiders alike.

Hart’s candid reflection on her artistic evolution and the forthcoming collaboration underscores her continued relevance in the contemporary music scene. As the release date for *Echoes of the Heart* approaches, listeners anticipate both the personal storytelling that defines the album and the potential impact of the rumored partnership with a rock legend.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Eddie Jones Uses Geese Videos to Motivate Japan Rugby
content:
Eddie Jones, the head coach of Japan’s national rugby team, has disclosed an unconventional pre‑match routine he employs before the side’s second Test against Australia. In a recent interview, Jones explained that he watches videos of geese flying in formation to inspire his players, using the birds’ coordinated flight as a metaphor for teamwork and collective effort.

The technique is part of Jones’s broader approach to building cohesion on the field. By observing how the geese maintain alignment and support one another while navigating the wind, he aims to translate those principles into on‑field communication, spatial awareness, and mutual trust among the Japanese squad. The method underscores the coach’s belief that visual, non‑rugby examples can reinforce the mental and tactical aspects of the game.

As Japan prepares to face a formidable Australian side, Jones’s creative coaching tools highlight his commitment to fostering unity and resilience within the team. The upcoming Test will test whether the lessons drawn from the skies translate into performance on the pitch.
author: BBC Sport

title: UK Economy Grows 0.4% in June, Sun and World Cup Boost Growth
content:
The United Kingdom's economy expanded by 0.4% in June, supported by favorable seasonal factors that stimulated activity across multiple sectors. This monthly growth rate reflects a positive contribution to national output, with businesses citing specific external drivers that enhanced consumer spending and commercial operations during the period.

Reports from various firms indicate that unseasonably hot weather and a schedule of major sporting events played a significant role in driving this economic performance. These conditions encouraged increased participation in leisure and travel-related activities, providing a temporary boost to industries that benefit from higher footfall and tourism, thereby contributing directly

title: Uniaxial Strain Enables Control of Electron Flow in Altermagnet
content: Researchers at Rice University have achieved a significant milestone in the study of altermagnetism, a newly identified third form of magnetism that holds substantial promise for next-generation spin-transport technologies. The breakthrough, detailed in a recent paper published in *Physical Review X*, marks the first successful manipulation of a proposed altermagnetic material

content:
